newsitem.title: BOSNIA: OSCE extends some Bosnia voting by three hours.
newsitem.headline: OSCE extends some Bosnia voting by three hours.

text.p: Some polling stations in Bosnia's elections will be kept open three hours past the official 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) close of voting on Saturday, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe said.
The OSCE, supervising Bosnia's first countrywide post-war elections, said difficulties experienced by voters in finding their names on polling station lists prompted its decision to extend voting.
One balloting centre in each of Bosnia's 109 opstinas, or municipalities, could stay open until 10 p.m. (2000 GMT) on Saturday, OSCE elections director Jeff Fischer told reporters.
All other polling places will formally close at 7 p.m. However, anyone still queueing up to vote at any station at 7 or 10 p.m. will be allowed to do so, he said.
Fischer told Reuters earlier that voter turnout was "moderate" by mid-afternoon but he gave no figures.
Numerous early delays were reported because of problems finding names on registration lists and the need to explain complex ballot forms and secret-vote procedures to some voters.
